title: Crypto Puzzles 2018: Puzzle #2
series: Crypto Puzzles (2018 YouTube channel), same series as the solved Puzzle #1

author.name: unnamed, published under the YouTube channel "Crypto Puzzles"

prize.note: single externally-owned account, never signed a transaction (nonce 0); that this address is Puzzle #2's escrow is a strong inference from the funder and amount matching Puzzle #1, not stated directly by the author

target_format: 64-character hex private key (32 bytes), secp256k1, Keccak-256 of the uncompressed public key to a 20-byte address, no BIP39, no passphrase, no derivation path

derivation.summary: read a 64-character hex private key hidden as composite glyphs across the two Puzzle #2 videos, then derive secp256k1 -> Keccak-256 -> last 20 bytes to an Ethereum address
derivation.certified_against: Puzzle #1's own published solution (64-hex answer read from its solution video), which derives to the address that received and was later spent from for that puzzle's own 0.05 ETH prize in 2018

difficulty_note: 16 of 64 characters are recovered and reproduce across two independent codecs. Three independent lines suggest the remaining 48 were never published: Puzzle 2 contains no flash frames where Puzzle 1 used them for the bulk of its key, Part 1 spends a whole seam on redundancy, and a 2018 commenter reported the same 16 characters and asked for a next part that never came.

leads.title: the three coordinates address an 8x8 grid
the four screen edges specify four block transforms
identify the unattributed video clip in Part 2

third_party_material: No video frames, screenshots, or video files are included; both puzzles are linked by video ID only. The certification vector (Puzzle #1's already-solved private key) is drawn from the author's own public solution video for a prize claimed and spent by an unrelated third party in 2018.
